SSH credential spray against PeopleSoft administrative accounts (psoft, oracle, linuxadm) AIInstallation High
Detects SSH authentication attempts targeting the three accounts the ShinyHunters lateral-movement script enumerates. The script tries password auth first then falls back to keys, so we alert on a single source generating both successful AND failed auth events against any of these usernames within a short window. Rationale: Article describes the script parsing /etc/hosts to find PeopleSoft hosts and attempting SSH with exactly these three usernames — psoft, oracle, linuxadm — before falling back to key-based auth. The username triplet plus multi-host fan-out is article-specific and not a generic SSH brute-force template. Cross-checked Oracle PeopleSoft installation guides confirming 'psoft' and 'oracle' as the standard install accounts. Cross-checked against: • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/oracle-peoplesoft-servers-hacked-in-shinyhunters-data-theft-attacks/ • https://docs.oracle.com/cd/F36211_01/psft/pdf/PT859TIBM-b1119.pdf
ATT&CKT1110.003 T1078.003 T1021.004
Data sourcesAuthentication
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Ansible/Chef/Puppet runs using the oracle account against multiple PeopleSoft hosts in the same batch window
  • Backup tooling (rsync, RMAN) authenticating as oracle to peer hosts
  • DBA bastion-host shell sessions hopping between PeopleSoft tier-1 and tier-2 servers
  • PeopleSoft application-server restart playbooks that SSH into every web tier
  • Pentest exercises authorised by the customer
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has_any ("ansible","puppet","chef-client","saltstack","rmanbackup")
Response runbook
1. Triage: enumerate the source IP — confirm whether it is internal (compromised peer) or external. If internal, treat that host as already-breached; if external, cross-reference against the seven IOC IPs. Pull historical successful logons for the same source across the prior 30 days. 2. Contain: rotate the password and SSH key material for psoft / oracle / linuxadm on every PeopleSoft host (and any host where these accounts also exist). Disable password authentication on PeopleSoft sshd_config if not already done. Add firewall rules restricting SSH ingress to bastion-only. 3. Hunt: review .bash_history of all three accounts on every targeted host, look for the ShinyHunters ransom-note filename, and check whether /etc/hosts itself was read by an unusual process (cat/grep/awk parented by sshd or bash from an external SSH session).
DeviceLogonEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(24h)
| where Protocol =~ "Ssh" or InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("sshd","sshd-session")
| where AccountName in~ ("psoft","oracle","linuxadm")
| summarize Attempts = count(),
            Successes = countif(ActionType =~ "LogonSuccess"),
            Failures = countif(ActionType =~ "LogonFailed"),
            TargetHosts = dcount(DeviceName),
            HostList = make_set(DeviceName, 25),
            UserList = make_set(AccountName, 10),
            FirstSeen = min(Timestamp),
            LastSeen = max(Timestamp)
            by RemoteIP
| where TargetHosts >= 2 or (Failures >= 5 and Successes >= 1)
| order by LastSeen desc
let badIPs = dynamic(["142.11.200.186","142.11.200.187","142.11.200.188","142.11.200.189","142.11.200.190","108.174.202.99","176.120.22.24"]);
let psoftAccounts = dynamic(["psoft","oracle","linuxadm"]);
union isfuzzy=true
  (Syslog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
    | where Facility in ("auth","authpriv") or ProcessName =~ "sshd"
    | where SyslogMessage has_any (psoftAccounts)
    | extend User = extract(@"(?i)user[= ]([A-Za-z0-9._-]+)", 1, SyslogMessage),
             SrcIP = extract(@"from\s+([0-9a-f:.]+)", 1, SyslogMessage),
             Outcome = case(SyslogMessage has "Accepted", "success", SyslogMessage has_any ("Failed","Invalid user","authentication failure"), "failure", "other")
    | where User in~ (psoftAccounts)
    | project TimeGenerated, Host = Computer, User, SrcIP, Outcome, SyslogMessage),
  (ImAuthentication
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
    | where LogonProtocol =~ "SSH" or EventProduct =~ "OpenSSH" or TargetAppName =~ "sshd"
    | where TargetUsername in~ (psoftAccounts)
    | project TimeGenerated, Host = DvcHostname, User = TargetUsername, SrcIP = SrcIpAddr, Outcome = EventResult, SyslogMessage = EventResultDetails)
| summarize Attempts = count(),
            Successes = countif(Outcome =~ "success" or Outcome =~ "Success"),
            Failures = countif(Outcome =~ "failure" or Outcome =~ "Failure"),
            TargetHosts = dcount(Host),
            HostList = make_set(Host, 25),
            UserList = make_set(User, 5),
            FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated),
            LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated)
            by SrcIP
| where TargetHosts >= 2 or (Failures >= 5 and Successes >= 1) or SrcIP in (badIPs)
| order by LastSeen desc
(source:linux.syslog OR source:linux.auditd OR source:okta) (@process.name:sshd OR @SyslogFacility:auth OR @evt.name:user.session.start) (@usr.id:(psoft OR oracle OR linuxadm) OR @user.name:(psoft OR oracle OR linuxadm) OR @TargetUsername:(psoft OR oracle OR linuxadm) OR @actor.alternateId:(psoft OR oracle OR linuxadm))
#event_simpleName=UserLogon
| LogonType=Network OR LogonType=Interactive OR LogonType=RemoteInteractive OR AuthenticationPackage=/ssh/i
| in(field=UserName, values=["psoft","oracle","linuxadm"]) OR in(field=RemoteAccount, values=["psoft","oracle","linuxadm"])
| groupBy([RemoteAddressIP4, UserName], function={
    count() as Attempts,
    count(field=aid, distinct=true) as TargetHostCount,
    min(_time) as FirstSeen,
    max(_time) as LastSeen
  })
| TargetHostCount >= 2
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count values(Authentication.action) as actions values(Authentication.dest) as dest_hosts dc(Authentication.dest) as host_count dc(Authentication.user) as user_count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Authentication where Authentication.app="sshd" AND Authentication.user IN ("psoft","oracle","linuxadm") by Authentication.src Authentication.user | `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)` | where host_count>=2 OR (user_count>=2) | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count values(Authentication.action) as actions values(Authentication.dest) as dest_hosts dc(Authentication.dest) as host_count dc(Authentication.user) as user_count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Authentication where Authentication.app="sshd" AND Authentication.user IN ("psoft","oracle","linuxadm") by Authentication.src Authentication.user | `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)` | where host_count>=2 OR (user_count>=2) | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
MeshCentral agent installation on Oracle PeopleSoft Linux servers AIInstallation Medium
Hunts for MeshCentral remote-management agent binaries or service installs on hosts identifying as PeopleSoft servers. The ShinyHunters staging directory included MeshCentral agents, indicating the actor uses MeshCentral as a backdoor / RMM C2 channel rather than dropping bespoke malware. Rationale: The article explicitly says Michael R found MeshCentral agents in the exposed ShinyHunters staging directories. MeshCentral binaries and command-line flags such as --meshServiceName / meshcentral.com beaconing are documented in the public MeshCentral source. We hunt rather than alert because MeshCentral is also a legitimate RMM — cross-checked the MeshCentral project documentation and the abuse.ch URLhaus listings for MeshCentral C2 panels. Cross-checked against: • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/oracle-peoplesoft-servers-hacked-in-shinyhunters-data-theft-attacks/ • https://github.com/Ylianst/MeshCentral • https://urlhaus.abuse.ch/
ATT&CKT1219 T1543.002 T1105
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • IT operations using MeshCentral as a sanctioned RMM tool for endpoint management
  • Schools running MeshCentral student-lab management (article notes education is most-affected sector)
  • Vendor support technicians authorised to remote into PeopleSoft tier servers via MeshCentral
  • Existing detection-engineering or red-team test environments running MeshCentral as part of C2 lab exercises
Suppression filter
| where not (DeviceName has_any ("itops-","helpdesk-","rmm-") and InitiatingProcessAccountName in~ ("sccm","ansible","itadmin"))
Response runbook
1. Triage: identify whether MeshCentral is an approved tool in this environment (ask IT). If approved, verify the install path, parent process, and the configured server domain match the sanctioned deployment. If unapproved or pointing at azurenetfiles.net / one of the seven IOC IPs, treat as confirmed C2. 2. Contain: kill the meshagent process, remove the systemd unit / Windows service, block the agent's configured server IP and azurenetfiles.net at the perimeter, snapshot the host, and rotate all local credentials. 3. Hunt: enumerate every host where the meshagent binary or its install path exists, pivot the agent's server hostname against DNS logs org-wide, and check for the ShinyHunters ransom-note file and SSH key-based logons to the same host.
let MeshIndicators = dynamic(["meshagent","meshservice","meshcmd","meshcentral","meshcentral.com","meshcentral2"]);
union
  (DeviceProcessEvents
   | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
   | where FileName in~ ("meshagent","meshagent.exe","meshservice","meshservice.exe","meshcmd","meshcmd.exe")
        or ProcessCommandLine has_any (MeshIndicators)
        or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any (MeshIndicators)
   | project Timestamp, EventType = "Process", DeviceName, AccountName,
             Image = FolderPath, Cmd = ProcessCommandLine,
             ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath, ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, SHA256),
  (DeviceFileEvents
   | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
   | where FileName in~ ("meshagent","meshagent.exe","meshservice","meshservice.exe","meshcmd")
        or FolderPath has_any ("/usr/local/mesh","/opt/meshcentral","meshagent","MeshCentral")
   | project Timestamp, EventType = "File", DeviceName, AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName,
             Image = FolderPath, Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
             ParentImage = InitiatingProcessParentFileName, ParentCmd = "", SHA256)
| order by Timestamp desc
let MeshIndicators = dynamic(["meshagent","meshservice","meshcmd","meshcentral","meshcentral.com","meshcentral2"]);
union isfuzzy=true
  (ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where ActingProcessName has_any (MeshIndicators) or TargetProcessName has_any (MeshIndicators) or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any (MeshIndicators) or TargetProcessCommandLine has_any (MeshIndicators)
    | project TimeGenerated, _Source = "ImProcessCreate", Host = DvcHostname, User = ActorUsername, Image = TargetProcessName, Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, ParentImage = ActingProcessName, ParentCmd = ActingProcessCommandLine),
  (ImFileEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where TargetFileName has_any (MeshIndicators) or TargetFilePath has_any ("/usr/local/mesh","/opt/meshcentral","meshagent","MeshCentral")
    | project TimeGenerated, _Source = "ImFileEvent", Host = DvcHostname, User = ActorUsername, Image = TargetFilePath, Cmd = ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentImage = ActingProcessName, ParentCmd = ""),
  (Syslog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where SyslogMessage has_any (MeshIndicators)
    | project TimeGenerated, _Source = "Syslog", Host = Computer, User = "", Image = SyslogMessage, Cmd = SyslogMessage, ParentImage = ProcessName, ParentCmd = "")
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: MeshCentral Agent Indicators on PeopleSoft Hosts
id: 5c419b67-2f8a-4a91-bd6e-8e3d5a91c0a2
description: Detects MeshCentral agent binaries, install paths, or command-line indicators consistent with ShinyHunters PeopleSoft staging.
references:
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/oracle-peoplesoft-servers-hacked-in-shinyhunters-data-theft-attacks/
author: SOC Detection Engineering

tags:

  - attack.t1219
logsource:
  category: process_creation
detection:
  selection_image:
    Image|contains:
      - 'meshagent'
      - 'MeshAgent'

  selection_cmd:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'meshcentral'
      - 'meshcentral.com'
      - 'meshcentral2'
      - '--meshServiceName'
  condition: selection_image or selection_cmd
level: medium
(source:windows.sysmon OR source:windows.security OR source:linux.auditd) (@Image:(*meshagent* OR *MeshAgent* OR *MeshService* OR *meshcmd*) OR @CommandLine:(*meshcentral* OR *meshcentral.com* OR *meshcentral2* OR *--meshServiceName*) OR @process.executable.path:(*meshagent* OR *meshservice* OR *meshcmd*) OR @process.command_line:(*meshcentral* OR *meshcentral.com* OR *--meshServiceName*))
(#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 OR #event_simpleName=FileWritten)
| (ImageFileName=/mesh(agent|service|cmd)/i OR TargetFileName=/mesh(agent|service|cmd)/i OR CommandLine=/meshcentral(\.com|2)?/i OR CommandLine=/--meshServiceName/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ImageFileName, TargetFileName, CommandLine, UserName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmdlines values(Processes.parent_process_name) as parents values(Processes.user) as users from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name IN ("meshagent","MeshAgent","MeshService","meshcmd") OR Processes.process IN ("*meshagent*","*MeshCentral*","*meshcentral.com*","*meshcentral2*") OR Processes.process="*--meshServiceName*") by Processes.dest Processes.process_name host | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmdlines values(Processes.parent_process_name) as parents values(Processes.user) as users from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name IN ("meshagent","MeshAgent","MeshService","meshcmd") OR Processes.process IN ("*meshagent*","*MeshCentral*","*meshcentral.com*","*meshcentral2*") OR Processes.process="*--meshServiceName*") by Processes.dest Processes.process_name host | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
DNS lookup or TLS SNI for ShinyHunters azurenetfiles.net infrastructure AICommand & Control High
Detects DNS or TLS-SNI traffic referencing the azurenetfiles.net domain, which the article ties to the ShinyHunters TLS certificate served by the IOC IP set. The domain has no legitimate use and predates this campaign in prior ShinyHunters operations. Rationale: Article reports that several of the IOC IPs served a TLS certificate whose common name is azurenetfiles.net, and notes the domain has been previously linked to ShinyHunters. Any DNS resolution or TLS-SNI hit on this domain inside an enterprise is high-fidelity. Cross-checked against MITRE ATT&CK G1015 (ShinyHunters) and the BleepingComputer prior coverage that ties azurenetfiles.net to the group. Cross-checked against: • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/oracle-peoplesoft-servers-hacked-in-shinyhunters-data-theft-attacks/ • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1015/ • https://threatfox.abuse.ch/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004 T1573
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Web.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Threat-intel scrapers / sandbox detonations resolving the domain for telemetry
  • Researcher VMs or DFIR analysts manually nslooking up the IOC
  • URL filtering proxies pre-resolving categorisation lookups
  • Internal documentation tools that automatically resolve any URL strings pasted into tickets
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","NisSrv.exe","SenseIR.exe")
Response runbook
1. Triage: identify the querying host and the process that made the request — if it's a browser the lookup is likely a user clicking a phishing link; if it's a service or LOLBin it's likely C2. Cross-reference the source host against the seven IOC IPs from the network-traffic UC. 2. Contain: sinkhole or NXDOMAIN azurenetfiles.net (and its known subdomains) at the resolver, block all seven IOC IPs at the perimeter, and isolate the querying host pending triage. 3. Hunt: pull the full process tree on the querying host, look for MeshCentral binaries, SSH outbound to peer PeopleSoft systems, and the ransom-note filename across the estate.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteUrl has "azurenetfiles.net" or RemoteUrl endswith ".azurenetfiles.net"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
  (DnsEvents
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where Name has "azurenetfiles.net"
    | project TimeGenerated, _Source = "DnsEvents", Host = Computer, ClientIP, Query = Name, ResponseCode = ResultCode, Answer = Result),
  (ImDnsActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where DnsQuery has "azurenetfiles.net"
    | project TimeGenerated, _Source = "ImDnsActivity", Host = SrcHostname, ClientIP = SrcIpAddr, Query = DnsQuery, ResponseCode = DnsResponseCodeName, Answer = DnsResponseName),
  (CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where DestinationDnsDomain has "azurenetfiles.net" or RequestURL has "azurenetfiles.net" or DestinationHostName has "azurenetfiles.net"
    | project TimeGenerated, _Source = "CommonSecurityLog", Host = SourceHostName, ClientIP = SourceIP, Query = coalesce(DestinationDnsDomain, DestinationHostName, RequestURL), ResponseCode = EventOutcome, Answer = DestinationIP)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium

Likely
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code.

Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Network connections to article IPs / domains

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["16562974deec80e41ef57a71a6de8c03ceb393005fb1432f8d9d82c61294ef8c", "1b2555b09ac62164638f47c8272beb6b0f97186e37d3a54cb84c723ff7a2eee5", "062bb28765fbaa11f8cc341fa16e2c7f942a122d929cb41f4a0f755b4429f246", "c7425fbe6c3a4937934215c54027d4b67202d12ab490682fae03498870d66d06", "a460d00ef93c8ce70d32e48e55781af66a53328fc2dde45519be196c265de074", "db2d33c4e6e4a5c2263b56e8303c343305a94dde1fc2968304ba260acbbd9f9f", "cf3f8160eb5a5580e0c35054847e3ac4d01e9fe74fab8bc12bf6e8a40bf696b2", "69077fcf940fc5852fb32beed15636756ebc04ac971b7ed71d36251e7ea70a20", "2ee93ccbcd49ed94c65dcf52e7dcb8f0fa0a443ca24c0e0c7f79152efba657b7", "9ff07c9fafa9c03fdf69e4abf6806aa7c938b5480e7e258f227db0719ecd6386", "7035c2abeb617e828dfda1b119b8544fa9ae15a1d263d18bc5506acaf381f496", "e021662a652ba95c8778b991056696ab3c9b0f60d5e23b1e6cf73c3847db6610"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Actions on Objectives
Likely
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha)
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: FakeCaptcha / ClickFix - Clipboard-Injected PowerShell from Explorer
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d06
status: experimental
description: |
    "FakeCaptcha" / "ClickFix" social-engineering: malicious site asks
    user to press Win+R and paste a payload. The result is
    powershell/mshta launched directly from explorer.exe with iex /
    base64 / downloadstring in the command line.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1204.002
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\explorer.exe'
            - '\RuntimeBroker.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
    selection_cmd:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'iex'
            - 'invoke-expression'
            - 'frombase64'
            - 'downloadstring'
            - 'hxxp'
            - 'curl '
            - 'wget '
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_cmd
falsepositives:
    - IT-driven scripted automation that admins paste-launch
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("185b7a487316454da04e9cc0fe6eb370bb2955cf6096fe3e8c02c46f8989ba37", "4c9061a07d667bf7dd6f597a43a8552af2f4277b7be06d6ea138abdb668d6a49", "949acbe543fc244ffbc981ea169067da7c5792af3c3d19b2c31b3d7e19106880", "be31a63cad112723178289968ad6f93a576c5a7984099c42eec3521cdf6e5fc0", "7d87a86dbd2379ef2516c99258137cd9c25ca19c48aeb096c5332c02fcbf16d0", "3a8f6454927b8993aded75de0de2bd00", "e83ff54e58f0b295a392c7fc39a7d0de", "b498256cb086a6962077cdd6d2f65327") or SHA1 in~ ("185b7a487316454da04e9cc0fe6eb370bb2955cf6096fe3e8c02c46f8989ba37", "4c9061a07d667bf7dd6f597a43a8552af2f4277b7be06d6ea138abdb668d6a49", "949acbe543fc244ffbc981ea169067da7c5792af3c3d19b2c31b3d7e19106880", "be31a63cad112723178289968ad6f93a576c5a7984099c42eec3521cdf6e5fc0", "7d87a86dbd2379ef2516c99258137cd9c25ca19c48aeb096c5332c02fcbf16d0", "3a8f6454927b8993aded75de0de2bd00", "e83ff54e58f0b295a392c7fc39a7d0de", "b498256cb086a6962077cdd6d2f65327") or MD5 in~ ("185b7a487316454da04e9cc0fe6eb370bb2955cf6096fe3e8c02c46f8989ba37", "4c9061a07d667bf7dd6f597a43a8552af2f4277b7be06d6ea138abdb668d6a49", "949acbe543fc244ffbc981ea169067da7c5792af3c3d19b2c31b3d7e19106880", "be31a63cad112723178289968ad6f93a576c5a7984099c42eec3521cdf6e5fc0", "7d87a86dbd2379ef2516c99258137cd9c25ca19c48aeb096c5332c02fcbf16d0", "3a8f6454927b8993aded75de0de2bd00", "e83ff54e58f0b295a392c7fc39a7d0de", "b498256cb086a6962077cdd6d2f65327")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("185b7a487316454da04e9cc0fe6eb370bb2955cf6096fe3e8c02c46f8989ba37", "4c9061a07d667bf7dd6f597a43a8552af2f4277b7be06d6ea138abdb668d6a49", "949acbe543fc244ffbc981ea169067da7c5792af3c3d19b2c31b3d7e19106880", "be31a63cad112723178289968ad6f93a576c5a7984099c42eec3521cdf6e5fc0", "7d87a86dbd2379ef2516c99258137cd9c25ca19c48aeb096c5332c02fcbf16d0", "3a8f6454927b8993aded75de0de2bd00", "e83ff54e58f0b295a392c7fc39a7d0de", "b498256cb086a6962077cdd6d2f65327") or SHA1 in~ ("185b7a487316454da04e9cc0fe6eb370bb2955cf6096fe3e8c02c46f8989ba37", "4c9061a07d667bf7dd6f597a43a8552af2f4277b7be06d6ea138abdb668d6a49", "949acbe543fc244ffbc981ea169067da7c5792af3c3d19b2c31b3d7e19106880", "be31a63cad112723178289968ad6f93a576c5a7984099c42eec3521cdf6e5fc0", "7d87a86dbd2379ef2516c99258137cd9c25ca19c48aeb096c5332c02fcbf16d0", "3a8f6454927b8993aded75de0de2bd00", "e83ff54e58f0b295a392c7fc39a7d0de", "b498256cb086a6962077cdd6d2f65327") or MD5 in~ ("185b7a487316454da04e9cc0fe6eb370bb2955cf6096fe3e8c02c46f8989ba37", "4c9061a07d667bf7dd6f597a43a8552af2f4277b7be06d6ea138abdb668d6a49", "949acbe543fc244ffbc981ea169067da7c5792af3c3d19b2c31b3d7e19106880", "be31a63cad112723178289968ad6f93a576c5a7984099c42eec3521cdf6e5fc0", "7d87a86dbd2379ef2516c99258137cd9c25ca19c48aeb096c5332c02fcbf16d0", "3a8f6454927b8993aded75de0de2bd00", "e83ff54e58f0b295a392c7fc39a7d0de", "b498256cb086a6962077cdd6d2f65327")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["185b7a487316454da04e9cc0fe6eb370bb2955cf6096fe3e8c02c46f8989ba37", "4c9061a07d667bf7dd6f597a43a8552af2f4277b7be06d6ea138abdb668d6a49", "949acbe543fc244ffbc981ea169067da7c5792af3c3d19b2c31b3d7e19106880", "be31a63cad112723178289968ad6f93a576c5a7984099c42eec3521cdf6e5fc0", "7d87a86dbd2379ef2516c99258137cd9c25ca19c48aeb096c5332c02fcbf16d0", "3a8f6454927b8993aded75de0de2bd00", "e83ff54e58f0b295a392c7fc39a7d0de", "b498256cb086a6962077cdd6d2f65327"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

JDY Linux shell dropper — architecture-aware MIPS/MIPSEL payload retrieval AIInstallation High
Hunts for the JDY first-stage shell dropper behavior on Linux SOHO/IoT/edge hosts: a curl/wget/tftp invocation that pulls a payload whose URL or filename embeds one of the architecture tokens (mips, mips64, mipsel, mipsel64) the dropper uses to select the right binary. Highly article-specific because the dropper enumerates exactly this set. Rationale: Anchors on the exact architecture-token set the article calls out (mips, mips64, mipsel, mipsel64) inside a download tool's cmdline — a combination that doesn't appear in benign sysadmin/package-manager activity. Corroborated against Lumen Black Lotus Labs' KV-botnet writeup (same MIPS-router targeting) and BleepingComputer's reporting on the JDY expansion. Cross-checked against: • https://blog.lumen.com/kv-botnet-dont-call-it-a-comeback/ • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/china-linked-jdy-botnet-expands-targeting-of-us-military-networks/ • https://blog.lumen.com/routers-roasting-on-an-open-firewall-the-kv-botnet-investigation/
ATT&CKT1105 T1059.004 T1027.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • OpenWrt/DD-WRT firmware update scripts pulling MIPS images by architecture name
  • Embedded-systems developers cross-compiling/downloading test binaries for MIPS targets onto Linux jump hosts
  • Yocto/Buildroot CI workers fetching MIPS toolchains over HTTP
  • Network appliance vendor maintenance scripts that name-tag firmware by architecture
  • Researchers/reverse-engineers downloading public malware samples for analysis from MalwareBazaar/VX-Underground
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("apt","apt-get","dpkg","yum","dnf","opkg","pacman","zypper","snap")
| where InitiatingProcessParentFileName !in~ ("apt","unattended-upgrades","buildroot","yocto")
Response runbook
Step 1 (Triage): Pull the parent process tree — confirm whether the curl/wget was launched by a legitimate package manager (apt/yum/opkg) or by an interactive shell / cron / unknown parent. Resolve the destination URL and check it against Black Lotus Labs' JDY IOC list on GitHub. Step 2 (Contain): If the host is a SOHO router, embedded device, or production server with no MIPS-development purpose, isolate from the network and snapshot for forensics — the binary self-deletes so capture /proc/<pid>/exe before kill. Step 3 (Hunt): Pivot on the destination IP/host across DeviceNetworkEvents (or ImNetworkSession) for the last 30 days to find sibling infections. Check for downstream high-fanout scanning from the host (UC #3).
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName in~ ("curl","wget","ftpget","tftp","busybox")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)\b(mips64|mipsel64|mipsel|mips)\b"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("http://","https://","://",".onion")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage = FileName,
          ChildCmd = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("curl","wget","ftpget","tftp","busybox")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)\b(mips64|mipsel64|mipsel|mips)\b"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("http://","https://","://",".onion")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine,
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, Hash
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: JDY Botnet Linux Dropper - MIPS Architecture Payload Fetch
id: 8b5a4d1c-3f72-4e89-9b14-2e7c5f8a1d36
description: Detects the JDY botnet first-stage shell dropper retrieving an architecture-specific payload (mips/mipsel/mips64/mipsel64) via curl/wget/tftp/busybox on Linux SOHO/IoT hosts.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/china-linked-jdy-botnet-expands-to-1500.html
  - https://blog.lumen.com/kv-botnet-dont-call-it-a-comeback/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/10
tags:
  - attack.t1105
  - attack.t1059.004
  - attack.command_and_control
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection_proc:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/curl'
      - '/wget'
      - '/ftpget'
      - '/tftp'
      - '/busybox'
  selection_arch:
    CommandLine|re: '(?i)\b(mips64|mipsel64|mipsel|mips)\b'
  selection_url:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'http://'
      - 'https://'
      - '.onion'
  condition: selection_proc and selection_arch and selection_url
level: high
source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:EXECVE (@process.name:(curl OR wget OR ftpget OR tftp OR busybox)) @process.command_line:(*mips* OR *mipsel* OR *mips64* OR *mipsel64*) @process.command_line:(*http\:\/\/* OR *https\:\/\/* OR *.onion*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 #event_platform=Lin
| ImageFileName=/(curl|wget|ftpget|tftp|busybox)$/i
| regex("(?i)\\b(mips64|mipsel64|mipsel|mips)\\b", field=CommandLine)
| regex("https?:\\/\\/|\\.onion", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmdline values(Processes.parent_process_name) as parent from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("curl","wget","ftpget","tftp","busybox") (Processes.process="*mips*" OR Processes.process="*mipsel*" OR Processes.process="*mips64*" OR Processes.process="*mipsel64*") (Processes.process="*http*" OR Processes.process="*://*" OR Processes.process="*.sh*") by host Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | rename host as dest | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmdline values(Processes.parent_process_name) as parent from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("curl","wget","ftpget","tftp","busybox") (Processes.process="*mips*" OR Processes.process="*mipsel*" OR Processes.process="*mips64*" OR Processes.process="*mipsel64*") (Processes.process="*http*" OR Processes.process="*://*" OR Processes.process="*.sh*") by host Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | rename host as dest | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
JDY botnet self-delete — Linux ELF executes then unlinks its own image AIActions on Objectives Medium
Hunts for the JDY post-execution defense-evasion behavior described in the article: the scanner binary is launched then deleted from disk so a live process has no on-disk backing file. Correlates a process-create on a non-system path with a delete of that same path within seconds. Rationale: The article explicitly states 'Once the malware is launched, it's deleted from disk' — a distinctive evasion the article calls out as a JDY characteristic. By joining process-create with same-path file-delete within a tight window, we surface this specific behavior on Linux hosts that ship Defender/ASIM telemetry without alerting on package-manager temp-file churn (filtered via the FP block). Cross-checked against: • https://blog.lumen.com/kv-botnet-dont-call-it-a-comeback/ • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/china-linked-jdy-botnet-expands-targeting-of-us-military-networks/
ATT&CKT1070.004 T1036.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Self-extracting installer shell archives (.run, makeself) in /tmp that extract → exec → cleanup
  • Ansible/Salt/Chef one-shot runners that drop a script in /tmp, execute, then remove
  • snapd / flatpak sandbox helpers in /var/run that are short-lived
  • CI runner ephemeral build steps inside /tmp/buildXXX
  • pip/npm post-install hooks that compile and clean up in /tmp
Suppression filter
| where ParentName !in~ ("sh","bash","dash") or true
| where not (ImagePath has_any ("/tmp/ansible-","/tmp/saltrun-","/tmp/build","/tmp/pip-","/tmp/npm-","/var/run/snapd/","/run/user/"))
Response runbook
Step 1 (Triage): For the matched process, dump /proc/<pid>/exe and /proc/<pid>/maps before the process exits — the deleted ELF is still mapped and can be recovered from memory. Capture the SHA256 and check against JDY samples on Black Lotus Labs' GitHub IOC repo. Step 2 (Contain): If recovered binary matches JDY tooling (or shows raw-socket SYN-scan code paths), isolate the host. Block any C2 IPs the live process is talking to (DeviceNetworkEvents → RemoteIP for that ProcessId). Step 3 (Hunt): Pivot on the parent process — JDY's dropper is a shell script; the parent should be /bin/sh or /bin/bash. Find the dropper invocation across the fleet and check for the architecture-specific payload pattern (UC #1).
let WindowSec = 30;
let ExecEvents = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where FolderPath has_any ("/tmp/","/var/tmp/","/dev/shm/","/var/run/","/run/")
    | project ExecTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, AccountName,
              ImagePath = FolderPath, ImageName = FileName,
              SHA256, ProcessCommandLine, ParentName = InitiatingProcessFileName;
let DeleteEvents = DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where ActionType in ("FileDeleted","FileRenamed")
    | where FolderPath has_any ("/tmp/","/var/tmp/","/dev/shm/","/var/run/","/run/")
    | project DelTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, DelPath = FolderPath, DelName = FileName,
              DelInitiator = InitiatingProcessFileName;
ExecEvents
| join kind=inner DeleteEvents on DeviceId
| where ImagePath == DelPath and ImageName == DelName
| extend GapSec = datetime_diff('second', DelTime, ExecTime)
| where GapSec between (0 .. WindowSec)
| project ExecTime, DelTime, GapSec, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ImagePath, ImageName, SHA256, ParentName, DelInitiator, ProcessCommandLine
| order by ExecTime desc
let WindowSec = 30;
let ExecEvents = ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where ActingProcessName has_any ("/tmp/","/var/tmp/","/dev/shm/","/var/run/","/run/")
    | project ExecTime = TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
              ImagePath = ActingProcessName, CmdLine = ActingProcessCommandLine,
              Hash;
let DeleteEvents = ImFileEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where EventType == "FileDeleted"
    | where TargetFilePath has_any ("/tmp/","/var/tmp/","/dev/shm/","/var/run/","/run/")
    | project DelTime = TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, DelPath = TargetFilePath;
ExecEvents
| join kind=inner DeleteEvents on DvcHostname
| where ImagePath == DelPath
| extend GapSec = datetime_diff('second', DelTime, ExecTime)
| where GapSec between (0 .. WindowSec)
| project ExecTime, DelTime, GapSec, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ImagePath, Hash, CmdLine
| order by ExecTime desc
source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:(EXECVE OR DELETE) @process.executable.path:(*/tmp/* OR */var/tmp/* OR */dev/shm/* OR */var/run/* OR */run/*) -@process.executable.path:*/snap/* -@process.executable.path:*/.cache/yarn/*
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 #event_platform=Lin ImageFileName=/^\/(tmp|var\/tmp|dev\/shm|var\/run|run)\//
| rename(field=ImageFileName, as=ExecPath)
| join({#event_simpleName=FileDeleted #event_platform=Lin TargetFileName=/^\/(tmp|var\/tmp|dev\/shm|var\/run|run)\//}, field=aid, key=aid, include=[TargetFileName, ContextImageFileName, _time], mode=inner)
| ExecPath = TargetFileName
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ExecPath], function=[count(), min(_time)])
ENDPOINT

| tstats summariesonly=true count from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_path IN ("/tmp/*","/var/tmp/*","/dev/shm/*","/var/run/*","/run/*") by _time host Processes.process_path Processes.process_name Processes.user | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | rename _time as procTime process_path as targetPath | join type=inner host targetPath [ | tstats summariesonly=true count from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.action="deleted" Filesystem.file_path IN ("/tmp/*","/var/tmp/*","/dev/shm/*","/var/run/*","/run/*") by _time host Filesystem.file_path | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | rename _time as delTime file_path as targetPath ] | eval gapSec=delTime-procTime | where gapSec >= 0 AND gapSec <= 30 | table procTime delTime gapSec host user process_name targetPath
| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_path IN ("/tmp/*","/var/tmp/*","/dev/shm/*","/var/run/*","/run/*") by _time host Processes.process_path Processes.process_name Processes.user | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | rename _time as procTime process_path as targetPath | join type=inner host targetPath [ | tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.action="deleted" Filesystem.file_path IN ("/tmp/*","/var/tmp/*","/dev/shm/*","/var/run/*","/run/*") by _time host Filesystem.file_path | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | rename _time as delTime file_path as targetPath ] | eval gapSec=delTime-procTime | where gapSec >= 0 AND gapSec <= 30 | table procTime delTime gapSec host user process_name targetPath
JDY-style reconnaissance — internal host high-fanout mixed-protocol scanning AIReconnaissance Medium
Detects a single internal host (likely a compromised SOHO/IoT device or jump box recruited into JDY) exhibiting the article's hallmark scanning shape: high-volume, simultaneous TCP/TLS/UDP/ICMP probing against many distinct external destinations in a short window. Tuned to fire on the rate + protocol-diversity + destination-fanout combination, which is the JDY tasking signature. Rationale: Article calls out the exact scanning shape: 'high-volume TCP, SSL, UDP, and ICMP-assisted probing' on the same node. Detecting that protocol mix combined with a fanout floor (200+ destinations, 20+ ports, <5 conn/dst mean) is far more article-specific than a generic 'noisy source' alert and is the JDY tasking signature. Corroborated against Lumen's KV-botnet writeup which describes identical mixed-protocol probing from the predecessor cluster. Cross-checked against: • https://blog.lumen.com/kv-botnet-dont-call-it-a-comeback/ • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/china-linked-jdy-botnet-expands-targeting-of-us-military-networks/ • https://blog.lumen.com/routers-roasting-on-an-open-firewall-the-kv-botnet-investigation/
ATT&CKT1595.002 T1046 T1584.005
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal vulnerability scanners (Nessus/Qualys/Rapid7 InsightVM/Tenable.io scan engines)
  • Internet measurement projects (Censys/Shodan-like scanners) running on a security research host
  • RUM/synthetic monitoring agents (Datadog, NewRelic) hitting many endpoints
  • MDM/EDR agents doing bulk policy refresh against many cloud endpoints
  • P2P clients on user laptops (BitTorrent DHT chatter looks similar)
Suppression filter
| where DeviceName !in~ ("nessus-scanner-01","qualys-engine-01","rapid7-engine-01")
| where not (DeviceName has_any ("scanner","probe","monitor"))
Response runbook
Step 1 (Triage): Identify the source DeviceName/SrcIpAddr — is it on the asset inventory? If yes, is it a sanctioned scanner (Nessus engine, internal probe)? Check OS/role: SOHO/IoT firmware, network appliance, IP camera, NVR are high-suspicion. Step 2 (Contain): If unsanctioned, network-isolate via NAC or 802.1X quarantine VLAN. For an IoT/SOHO device, power-cycle is rarely sufficient — JDY survives reboot per Lumen; pull the device and reimage. Step 3 (Hunt): Look for the dropper chain on this host (UC #1) and for outbound connections to Tor entry nodes from the same source. Pull DNS for the past 7 days from the host's resolver — JDY uses Tor relays as C2, so look for .onion lookups or known Tor consensus IPs.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1h)
| where ActionType in ("ConnectionAttempt","ConnectionSuccess","ConnectionFailed","InboundConnectionAccepted")
| where RemoteIPType == "Public"
| summarize 
    DistinctDsts = dcount(RemoteIP),
    DistinctPorts = dcount(RemotePort),
    DistinctProtos = dcount(Protocol),
    Protos = make_set(Protocol, 10),
    SamplePorts = make_set(RemotePort, 20),
    TotalConns = count()
    by DeviceName, DeviceId, bin(Timestamp, 5m)
| where DistinctDsts >= 200 and DistinctProtos >= 3 and DistinctPorts >= 20
| extend MeanConnsPerDst = TotalConns * 1.0 / DistinctDsts
| where MeanConnsPerDst < 5     // scanner shape: many destinations, few packets each
| order by Timestamp desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1h)
| where isnotempty(DstIpAddr) and DstIpAddr !startswith "10." and DstIpAddr !startswith "192.168." and DstIpAddr !startswith "172.16."
| summarize 
    DistinctDsts = dcount(DstIpAddr),
    DistinctPorts = dcount(DstPortNumber),
    DistinctProtos = dcount(NetworkProtocol),
    Protos = make_set(NetworkProtocol, 10),
    TotalConns = count()
    by SrcIpAddr, SrcHostname, bin(TimeGenerated, 5m)
| where DistinctDsts >= 200 and DistinctProtos >= 3 and DistinctPorts >= 20
| extend MeanConnsPerDst = TotalConns * 1.0 / DistinctDsts
| where MeanConnsPerDst < 5
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:3 @DestinationIp:* -@DestinationIp:(10.* OR 192.168.* OR 172.16.* OR 172.17.* OR 172.18.* OR 172.19.* OR 172.20.* OR 172.21.* OR 172.22.* OR 172.23.* OR 172.24.* OR 172.25.* OR 172.26.* OR 172.27.* OR 172.28.* OR 172.29.* OR 172.30.* OR 172.31.*)
#event_simpleName=/^NetworkConnectIP[46]$/
| ConnectionDirection=0 OR ConnectionDirection=1
| !cidr("10.0.0.0/8", field=RemoteAddressIP4) | !cidr("192.168.0.0/16", field=RemoteAddressIP4) | !cidr("172.16.0.0/12", field=RemoteAddressIP4)
| bucket(span=5m, field=_time, function={ groupBy([aid, ComputerName], function=[count(as=Total), count(field=RemoteAddressIP4, distinct=true, as=DistinctDsts), count(field=RemotePort, distinct=true, as=DistinctPorts), count(field=Protocol, distinct=true, as=DistinctProtos)]) })
| DistinctDsts >= 200
| DistinctProtos >= 3
| DistinctPorts >= 20

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High
Match vulnerability scanner output to the CVE(s) named in the article.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-35616")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-35616")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",

         by Processes.dest, Processes.user

Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) Exploitation High
Browser-pasted PowerShell launched from explorer/Run dialog — ClickFix social engineering.

Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)

title: FakeCaptcha / ClickFix - Clipboard-Injected PowerShell from Explorer
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d06
status: experimental
description: |
    "FakeCaptcha" / "ClickFix" social-engineering: malicious site asks
    user to press Win+R and paste a payload. The result is
    powershell/mshta launched directly from explorer.exe with iex /
    base64 / downloadstring in the command line.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1204.002
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\explorer.exe'
            - '\RuntimeBroker.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
    selection_cmd:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'iex'
            - 'invoke-expression'
            - 'frombase64'
            - 'downloadstring'
            - 'hxxp'
            - 'curl '
            - 'wget '
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_cmd
falsepositives:
    - IT-driven scripted automation that admins paste-launch
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"

Ivanti Sentry handleMessage endpoint exploitation (CVE-2026-10520) AIExploitation High
Hunts HTTP requests to the Ivanti Sentry MICS endpoint /mics/api/v2/sentry/mics-config/handleMessage, which watchTowr Labs identified as the unauthenticated RCE sink reaching the backend handleExecute() in CVE-2026-10520 (CVSS 10.0). Pre-patch, ANY hit on this endpoint from the internet (or from an unexpected internal source) is a candidate exploitation attempt; post-patch, hits should redirect to the login page so successful POSTs with 2xx are anomalous. Rationale: watchTowr Labs explicitly named /mics/api/v2/sentry/mics-config/handleMessage as the vulnerable endpoint reaching handleExecute() — this is a unique, non-generic path string that exists nowhere else legitimate on a Sentry appliance and produces near-zero baseline noise. The path is on the Sentry box itself so the gold telemetry is WAF/proxy logs (CommonSecurityLog/Datadog web sources), with the Defender query catching lateral exploitation attempts.
ATT&CKT1190 T1059
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Authorized vulnerability scanning (Tenable Nessus, Qualys, Rapid7 InsightVM, watchTowr ASM) probing the endpoint post-disclosure to confirm patch status
  • Internal red-team / purple-team exercises against the new CVE
  • Ivanti TAC support sessions where legitimate admin troubleshooting reaches the endpoint via VPN
  • Pre-prod / staging Sentry appliances being validated against pentest tooling
  • Synthetic monitoring scripts written by the platform team to verify the patch's redirect-to-login behavior
Suppression filter
// In Sentinel — exclude known scanner source IPs (maintain a Watchlist 'VulnScanners') and Ivanti support ASNs
| where SourceIP !in (toscalar(_GetWatchlist('VulnScanners') | summarize make_set(SourceIP)))
| where tostring(RequestClientApplication) !has_any ("Nessus", "Qualys", "InsightVM", "Nuclei", "watchTowr")
Response runbook
Step 1 — TRIAGE: Identify the source IP and confirm it is unauthenticated (no prior valid session cookie / Authorization header on requests from the same SourceIP within 1 hour). Pull the full POST body from the WAF log to look for shell metacharacters (`;`, `|`, `$(`, backticks). Check whether the Sentry appliance is patched to R10.5.2 / R10.6.2 / R10.7.1. Step 2 — CONTAIN: If unpatched and the request returned 2xx, block the source IP at the perimeter and isolate the Sentry appliance from the management network. Force expire all Sentry admin sessions and rotate any credentials/certificates the appliance brokers (MDM enrollment certs, SCEP, CA). Step 3 — HUNT: Pivot on the Sentry appliance's outbound connections in the 24h before/after the request — look for new reverse shells, cron jobs, or SSH keys on the appliance. Cross-check CVE-2026-10523 (auth bypass) for any newly-created admin accounts in the Sentry admin portal. Review MDM-managed device fleet for unauthorized profile pushes
// Catches lateral-pivot exploitation attempts where an internal endpoint hits the Sentry MICS endpoint.
// Inbound-from-internet exploitation must be caught via the Sentinel/WAF query — Sentry appliance does not ship to Defender.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteUrl has "/mics/api/v2/sentry/mics-config/handleMessage"
   or AdditionalFields has "/mics/api/v2/sentry/mics-config/handleMessage"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessAccountName, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Protocol
| order by Timestamp desc
// Primary surface: WAF / proxy / firewall logs forwarded as CEF.
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where RequestURL has "/mics/api/v2/sentry/mics-config/handleMessage"
| extend SuccessfulPost = (RequestMethod =~ "POST" and tostring(EventOutcome) startswith "2")
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct, SourceIP, SourceUserName,
          DestinationIP, DestinationHostName, RequestMethod, RequestURL, EventOutcome,
          RequestClientApplication, Activity, SuccessfulPost
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Ivanti Sentry MICS handleMessage Endpoint Access (CVE-2026-10520)
id: 6f4e2b50-2d4a-4c2f-9bca-1c0c7c4f5f02
description: Detects HTTP requests to the Ivanti Sentry /mics/api/v2/sentry/mics-config/handleMessage endpoint, the unauthenticated RCE sink in CVE-2026-10520 reaching the backend handleExecute() component. Post-patch, requests should be redirected to the login page; any successful POST is highly suspicious.

Vulnerable Ivanti / Fortinet / SAP versions exposed to June 2026 critical CVEs AIReconnaissance High
Inventory hunt across Defender TVM (and Sentinel's mirror of the same table) for assets running versions of Ivanti Sentry, FortiSandbox, SAP NetWeaver AS ABAP/Java, SAP Commerce Cloud, or SAP Data Hub that are vulnerable to the seven critical CVEs disclosed June 10 2026. Output is a prioritized patch worklist — these are the assets that will be exploited next if any of these CVEs get weaponized. Rationale: Article enumerates the exact affected versions (FortiSandbox 5.0.0–5.0.5 / 4.4.0–4.4.8, Ivanti Sentry pre-R10.5.2/R10.6.2/R10.7.1) and all seven CVE IDs. Defender TVM is the authoritative source for what's running where — this turns the patch advisory into an actionable worklist. Prioritization in the query reflects the CVSS hierarchy with CVE-2026-10520 (10.0, unauth RCE) at the top.
ATT&CKT1190 T1592.002
Data sources
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • TVM lag: assets patched in the last 24h still appearing as vulnerable until next scan cycle completes
  • Decommissioned / retired appliances still in TVM inventory (filter by Heartbeat / last-seen)
  • Non-production lab Sentry/SAP/FortiSandbox instances intentionally left unpatched for security testing
  • Vendor-managed appliances where the customer cannot apply patches directly (contact vendor instead)
Suppression filter
// Suppress retired / non-reporting devices
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(2d) | distinct DeviceId) on DeviceId
// Suppress lab tag if you label TVM with MachineGroup
| where MachineGroup !contains "lab" and MachineGroup !contains "sandbox-test"
Response runbook
Step 1 — TRIAGE: Sort the output by Priority then IsInternetFacing=true; the internet-facing P0 assets (CVE-2026-10520 unpatched Ivanti Sentry) are the queue. Cross-reference each PublicIP against attack-surface management to confirm exposure. Step 2 — CONTAIN: For internet-facing Ivanti Sentry on vulnerable versions, place a temporary WAF rule blocking POST to /mics/api/v2/sentry/mics-config/handleMessage until R10.5.2/R10.6.2/R10.7.1 is applied; coordinate emergency change windows with the MDM team. For FortiSandbox, restrict WEB UI access to management VLAN only pending 5.0.6 / 4.4.9 upgrade. Step 3 — HUNT: Once patched, run UC1 retroactively over the prior 90 days against the Sentry asset IPs to look for pre-disclosure exploitation. For SAP NetWeaver, additionally pull SAP Security Audit Log entries for RFC errors (CVE-2026-27671 telltale) and unusual SAML assertions (CVE-2026-44748).

DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
